title: feat(types,plugin-designer)!: draw the page and report designers' read members and every canvas background; a report field reads dataBinding; sweep the designer inputs (objectui#11434, PR 3 of 3)
body:
Fixes #11434

Clause-②: yes

This is PR 3 of 3, the final one, under the seat's ruling 5946170549 (staged option B, the "Read" section) and the seat's ACCEPT on PR 2 (5949189495). It gives readers to the remaining READ members: the page designer, the shared canvases and the report designer. It also sweeps every designer registration's `inputs`, which PR 2's ACCEPT carried here.

- PR 1 (objectui#11451) held every retirement.
- PR 2 (objectui#11454, merged into this branch before opening) gave readers to the data-model and process designers, plus the `onDelete` respelling.

After this PR, no member of the `@object-ui/plugin-designer` node family stays declared and unread.

## What draws each member

"Read" means the renderer draws it. Each row is pinned by a render probe through the real `SchemaRenderer` and registry that compares the drawn markup with the member set and unset. Each row also names WHAT is drawn. No pin rests on a style value alone. Colour, font and spacing are asserted through the class that paints them and the custom property that carries them.

| Member | Drawn as | Pin |
|---|---|---|
| `DesignerCanvasConfig.backgroundColor` | the canvas colour on the page, data-model and process canvases, via `--designer-canvas-bg` and a static `bg-[color:var(...)]` utility (the author-declared-colour carve-out) | `DesignerCanvas.backgroundColor-11434.test.tsx` |
| `DesignerComponent.children` | nested inside the parent box, positioned within it, and indented under it in the component tree. Select, edit, move, copy and delete reach nested components. | `PageDesigner.readers-11434.test.tsx` |
| `DesignerComponent.locked` | no drag, no canvas delete button, a lock marker | same |
| `DesignerComponent.visible` | `false` draws faded and dashed, with a hidden marker, so the component can still be found | same |
| `DesignerComponent.zIndex` | the component box's stacking order | same |
| `DesignerPaletteCategory.icon` | a Lucide glyph beside the category label, looked up through `resolveIcon` from `@object-ui/components` | same |
| `DesignerPaletteItem.icon` | the item's glyph in place of the generic "add" glyph, which remains the fallback | same |
| `DesignerPaletteItem.preview` | a thumbnail on the palette button | same |
| `ReportDesignerElement.dataBinding` | a field element draws `{BINDING}`, and any other element draws its binding beside its content. The property panel's **Data binding** entry edits it on every element, and a new field element is created bound. | `ReportDesigner.readers-11434.test.tsx` |
| `ReportDesignerElement.format` | weight, style, alignment and vertical alignment as utilities; colour, background, font size, font family, border and padding through custom properties and static utilities; `numberFormat` / `dateFormat` beside the binding | same (12 rows) |
| `ReportDesignerSection.groupField` | `by FIELD` in the section label | same |
| `ReportDesignerSection.pageBreakBefore` | a page-break rule across the top of the section | same |
| `ReportDesignerSchema.margins.top` / `.right` / `.bottom` | a dashed margin guide on the page, carrying all four sides | same |

The property panel of a page component also offers **Visible**, **Locked** and **Z-index**.

## `dataBinding` over `properties.field`

- **Producers, measured first.** `git grep` over this repository and ObjectStack found no doc, example, skill or ObjectStack producer of `properties.field`. Two places produced it:
  - `ReportDesigner` itself: a new field element was born with `properties.field: 'field_name'`, and the panel's Field entry wrote it;
  - one test fixture (`designer-zod-arms-10859`), which this PR rewrites to `properties: {}` beside its existing `dataBinding`.

  Documents a host saved from the designer can carry the key, so it gets a migration line and a loud refusal, not a silent drop.
- **Renderer.** The field element draws `dataBinding` alone. A pin proves that `properties.field` draws exactly what its absence draws: no fallback reads the bag key.
- **zod face, refused by name.** `ReportDesignerElementSchema.properties` stays a record, so a text element's `text` stays authorable on both validator faces. A check on the record reports `field` at its own path (`sections.N.elements.M.properties.field`, code `custom`), with the migration. I first wrote it as an object with a catchall. That was measured wrong, because the strict authoring face shuts every object it reaches and so refused `text` as an unrecognized key. Only a record stays open there.
- **TypeScript face, unchanged** (an open record of `string` keys to `unknown` values). Its docblock carries the migration. One key of an open bag cannot be refused in the type without parting from that record: a `field?: never` member made the faces unequal for the mirror-parity rows. A pin keeps the two faces equal.
- **Migration line.** Move the value to the element's `dataBinding`, and delete `properties.field`.

## The inputs sweep (`packages/plugin-designer/src/index.tsx`)

Measured first: `inputs` feeds the html-tier page compiler. Its manifest is built from every known registration, and its `validateTree` answers `unknown-prop` for a node key no input names. Against BASE inputs, a node carrying each read member drew these warnings:

- `process-designer`: `version`, `lanes`, `canvas`;
- `data-model-designer`: `canvas`, `showRelationshipLabels`;
- `page-designer`: `palette`, `propertyEditor`;
- `report-designer`: `pageSize`, `orientation`, `margins`.

At this head it draws none of them. The rows, one by one:

| Registration | Added rows | Why each is an input | Not an input, and why |
|---|---|---|---|
| `page-designer` | `palette` (array), `propertyEditor` (boolean) | both read by `PageDesigner`. `canvas` was already listed. | `body` / `children` (refused content channels) |
| `data-model-designer` | `canvas` (object), `showRelationshipLabels` (boolean) | both read | `body` / `children`; `autoLayout` (retired tombstone) |
| `process-designer` | `version` (string), `lanes` (array), `canvas` (object) | read since PR 2 (`canvas` was always read) | `body` / `children` |
| `report-designer` | `pageSize` and `orientation` (enum, the declared vocabularies), `margins` (object) | all three read: page size and orientation, and the margin guide | `body` / `children`; `previewMode` (retired tombstone) |
| `object-manager`, `field-designer` | none | every read member already listed | `body` / `children` |

Each added row declares the kind its value has, so a legal value draws no `type-mismatch`. `designerRegistrationInputs-11434.test.ts` pins each registration's input names to its read members, and pins the added kinds. The brief said no registration listed `canvas`; measured, `page-designer` did.

**Patch round 1 (seat order 5950875446): the `code` rows.** A `code` row is judged as a string, so `validateTree` answered `type-mismatch` ("expected a string") on every legal value of these pre-existing rows. Each is now declared by its value's kind, the objectui#10993 shape:

| Registration | Re-declared rows |
|---|---|
| `page-designer` | `canvas` (object), `components` (array) |
| `data-model-designer` | `entities`, `relationships` (array) |
| `process-designer` | `nodes`, `edges` (array) |
| `report-designer` | `sections` (array) |
| `object-manager` | `objects` (array) |
| `field-designer` | `fields` (array) |

No designer row is `code` any more. The pin now builds the html-tier manifest the way `page.tsx` does and runs `validateTree` over one legal document per designer, naming every input. It asserts no `type-mismatch` and no `unknown-prop`. A control row proves the instrument fires: a string `nodes` is a `type-mismatch`.

**Premise, verified first: who reads `inputs[].type` for these registrations.** I grepped every non-test reader of registration `inputs` across `packages/*` and `apps/*`.

- The only reader of these rows' kinds is the html-tier compile in `page.tsx` (`getJsxManifest`, then `manifestFromConfigs`, then `validateTree`'s `checkType`).
- `parse` uses no kind.
- The published `sdui.manifest.json`, `generateDts` and the `kind:'react'` scope (`react-page.tsx`) carry the public tier alone, and no designer is in it: none is in `PUBLIC_BLOCKS` or registers `tier: 'public'`.
- No studio inspector renders these rows by kind. The `code` widgets in `app-shell` are field-type widgets, not registry inputs.
- ObjectStack consumes only the published manifest.

So nothing regresses, and no row was kept back as a fork.

One measured nuance: `type-mismatch` and `unknown-prop` on these rows are WARNING-severity diagnostics, and `page.tsx` renders only errors. Neither the old `type-mismatch` nor the earlier `unknown-prop` ever reached a screen. The change makes the declarations true, and the pin judges the diagnostic itself. A string where an array is now declared draws a warning, never an error, so nothing that compiled before fails now.

## Ledgers

- Measured at BASE `0e9058b95`, after PR 2: `UnmirroredDeclared` holds 5 entries / 16 keys and **no designer entry**. PR 2 removed the last one. `EXPECTED_MIRROR_PAIRS` is 191.
- This PR adds no pair and mirrors nothing new: every member it gives a reader was already mirrored. So **no ledger figure moves**, and no ledger edit is in the diff.
- The only face-shape change is the check on `properties`, and its input type is unchanged, so no parity row moves.
- The `designer.zod.ts` header and the zod README now say every member of the family is drawn.
- The four "registration declares … as its inputs" sentences in `designer.ts` are updated to the swept rows.

## Changesets

- `@object-ui/types`: **minor**, with the **BREAKING (authoring)** banner for the `properties.field` refusal, `Clause-②: yes`, and the migration line.
- `@object-ui/plugin-designer`: **minor**, with a **BREAKING (rendering)** note: a field element no longer reads `properties.field`. The note carries the migration line. It also lists the new drawn output and the input rows.

- **Ablation A** (the canvas stops drawing `children`): predicted 1 red; observed **1 red** of 7.
- **Ablation B** (the field element falls back to `properties.field` before `dataBinding`, the alias read this PR refuses): predicted 1 red, the no-fallback row; observed **1 red** of 21.
- **Ablation C** (the record check stops looking for `field`): predicted 2 red, the two refusal rows with the control green; observed **2 red** of 3.
- **Landing and restore proofs.** Each mutation went through `ablation-replace.mjs` (anchor 1 → 0, blob moved) with an independent `grep -c`. Each was restored by `git checkout HEAD --` and proven by blob == HEAD and an empty `git diff HEAD`, and a trap re-proved all three.

## Patch round 2, at `f1f092146`

The contract record 5951435915 found that `locked` claimed a protection the code did not deliver. The seat ruled arm (a), make the sentence true (order 5951451514).

**Code.** `handleDeleteComponent` and `handleDeleteSelected` (Delete / Backspace and the toolbar's **Delete selected**) now skip a locked component. They also skip any parent that holds one anywhere inside it, because deleting the parent would take the locked component with it. The dialog counts only what it deletes. A selection that holds nothing deletable opens no dialog, and a parent holding a lock offers no delete button. The `DesignerComponent.locked` docblock and the changeset's `locked` bullet now state the nested behaviour. The table row above and the `renderComponent` comment are unchanged, as the order asked.

**Pins.** `PageDesigner.readers-11434` gains four rows:

- a selected locked component survives Delete;
- it survives **Delete selected**;
- the control: in the same selection, the unlocked sibling IS deleted, and the dialog says "1 component";
- a parent holding a locked child is kept and offers no delete button.
